title: WPSS/1615/2021 of SATEESH PRASAD UNIYAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No.1615 of 2021
With
WPSS No.1616 of 2021
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Shashank Saun, Advocate for the
petitioner.
Mr. Sushil Vashistha, Brief Holder for the
State of Uttarakhand.
In these two writ petitions the petitioners,
who are two and five in numbers respectively, have
prayed, that a writ of mandamus may be issued to
the respondents to grant them the time scale which
they are entitled to, after completing their ten years
of service which they have rendered from their
respective date of initial appointment and release
the benefit without any delay within the stipulated
time frame.
Simultaneously, a prayer has also been
sought for, that the respondents may be directed to
grant pensionary benefits under the Old Pension
Scheme, since the time when the petitioners of
WPSS No.1615 of 2021 were initially appointed in
Veer Chandra Singh Garhwali Junior High School,
Maikhada, Rudraprayag and petitioners of WPSS
No.1616 of 2021 were appointed in Nav Jyoti Janta
Junior High School Panyya, Development Block
Gairsain, Chamoli.
The petitioners have come up in the writ
petitions with the case, that the claim of the
petitioners stands covered by the judgment of the
Division Bench as rendered on 30.08.2018 in a
bunch of Special Appeal with the leading Special
Appeal No.279 of 2018, State of Uttarakhand and
others vs. Harish Singh Boha and others. As a
consequence, thereto, it has resulted into the
affirmation of the judgment of Learned Single
Judge dated 27.03.2017, which was under challenge
before the Division Bench.

Based on the principles enunciated by the
Division Bench, there had been several other writ
petitions, which had travelled before this Court for
eg. writ petition being Writ Petition (S/S) No.1538
of 2021, 1540 of 2021 and 1456 of 2021 they were
decided and based on the prime principle which has
been laid down by the Division Bench in the
judgment of 30.08.2018, the writ petitions were
disposed of by the respective judgments of
07.12.2021 and 18.11.2021 by this Court.
This is not in dispute by the respondents'
counsel, that the issue involved stands covered by
the aforesaid judgments and hence, the consensus
has been extended, that the matter may be disposed
of in the light of the subsequent judgments rendered
by this Court.
Hence, these writ petitions too would stand
disposed of in terms of the judgment dated
18.11.2021 rendered in Writ Petition (S/S) No.1456
of 2021; to be read with the judgment of the
Division Bench judgment dated 30.08.2018
rendered in Special Appeal No.279 of 2018, State
of Uttarakhand and others vs. Harish Singh Bora
and others.
Consequent thereto, the respondents are
directed to consider the claim of the petitioners and
take a decision on it within a period of six weeks
from the date of presentation of the certified copy
of this order.
Subject to the above observations, the writ
petitions stand disposed of.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 21.12.2021
